title: Cancer immunotherapy
why: Suzanne Topalian's team shows that an antibody blocking PD-1, one of the immune system's brakes, shrinks advanced lung, skin and kidney cancers in some patients, including lung cancer, long thought beyond the reach of immunotherapy.

title: CRISPR gene editing
why: Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier show that the Cas9 protein can be programmed with a guide RNA to cut any chosen DNA sequence, creating a simple tool for editing genes.

title: Higgs boson
why: Physicists at CERN's Large Hadron Collider find the Higgs boson, the particle predicted in 1964 that explains how other particles get their mass.

title: Denisovan genome
org: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology
why: Matthias Meyer and Svante Pääbo read the complete genome of the Denisovans, an extinct human group known only from a finger bone and teeth, as accurately as a living person's.

title: Eggs from stem cells
why: Katsuhiko Hayashi and Mitinori Saitou turn mouse stem cells into eggs that, once fertilized, grow into healthy, fertile pups.

title: Bounded prime gaps
why: Yitang Zhang proves that infinitely many pairs of primes sit less than 70 million apart, a first step toward the twin prime conjecture.

title: Weak Goldbach conjecture
why: Harald Helfgott proves that every odd number greater than 5 is the sum of three primes, settling the weak form of a question Goldbach posed in 1742.

title: Interstellar space
org: NASA JPL and University of Iowa
why: Don Gurnett's team shows that NASA's Voyager 1 left the Sun's bubble of particles in August 2012, making it the first human-made object in interstellar space.

title: Cosmic neutrinos
why: The IceCube detector buried in Antarctic ice catches the first high-energy neutrinos known to come from beyond the solar system.

title: Expanded genetic alphabet
why: Floyd Romesberg's team creates bacteria that keep and copy a man-made third pair of DNA letters alongside nature's two.

title: Lab-grown beta cells
why: Douglas Melton's team turns human stem cells into hundreds of millions of working insulin-making beta cells that control blood sugar in diabetic mice.

title: Comet landing
why: ESA's Rosetta mission sets its Philae lander down on comet 67P/Churyumov–Gerasimenko, the first soft landing on a comet.

title: Teixobactin
why: Kim Lewis and Slava Epstein's team grows soil bacteria that had never been cultured and finds teixobactin, a new kind of antibiotic that kills drug-resistant bacteria without them developing resistance.

title: Pluto
org: NASA, Johns Hopkins APL and SwRI
why: NASA's New Horizons, led by Alan Stern, flies past Pluto, the first spacecraft ever to visit it.

title: Ebola vaccine
org: WHO and Guinea's Ministry of Health
why: A ring-vaccination trial in Guinea led by Ana Maria Henao-Restrepo shows the rVSV-ZEBOV vaccine protects people from Ebola, the first vaccine proven to do so.

title: Loophole-free Bell test
why: Ronald Hanson's team runs the first Bell test with no loopholes, confirming that quantum entanglement's "spooky action at a distance" is real.

title: Orbital rocket landing
why: SpaceX lands a Falcon 9 first stage upright at Cape Canaveral after it helped launch satellites to orbit, the first time an orbital rocket's booster came back and landed.

title: Gravitational waves
why: LIGO, built on the work of Rainer Weiss, Kip Thorne and Barry Barish, detects ripples in space-time from two black holes colliding, confirming Einstein's century-old prediction.

title: Sphere packing
why: Maryna Viazovska proves the densest way to stack spheres in eight dimensions, and a week later she and four colleagues do the same in 24 dimensions.

title: Proxima b
org: Queen Mary University of London and ESO
why: Guillem Anglada-Escudé's team finds a roughly Earth-mass planet in the habitable zone of Proxima Centauri, the nearest star to the Sun.

title: Three-parent baby
why: John Zhang's team reveals the first baby born using spindle nuclear transfer, which combines DNA from three people to keep the mother's fatal mitochondrial disease from passing to her child.

title: Oldest Homo sapiens
org: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology and Morocco's INSAP
why: Jean-Jacques Hublin and Abdelouahed Ben-Ncer date Homo sapiens fossils from Jebel Irhoud, Morocco, to about 300,000 years ago, pushing our species' origin back by about 100,000 years.

title: Neutron star merger
why: For the first time, astronomers both detect the gravitational waves and see the light from two neutron stars colliding, showing that such crashes forge gold and other heavy elements.

title: Oumuamua
why: Robert Weryk spots Oumuamua, the first object ever seen passing through the solar system from another star.

title: SMA gene therapy
why: Jerry Mendell's team shows that a one-time gene therapy keeps babies with spinal muscular atrophy type 1, a disease usually fatal by age two, alive and reaching milestones like sitting up.

title: Magic-angle graphene
why: Yuan Cao and Pablo Jarillo-Herrero show that two sheets of graphene twisted to a "magic" angle of about 1.1 degrees become a superconductor.

title: Chromatic number of the plane
why: Amateur mathematician Aubrey de Grey proves that coloring the plane so that no two points one unit apart share a color takes at least five colors, the first progress on the problem since 1950.

title: Cosmic neutrino source
why: IceCube traces a high-energy neutrino back to a flaring galaxy, the blazar TXS 0506+056, the first known source of cosmic neutrinos.

title: Arrokoth
org: NASA, Johns Hopkins APL and SwRI
why: NASA's New Horizons, led by Alan Stern, flies past Arrokoth, then nicknamed Ultima Thule, the most distant object ever explored and the first close look at a primordial body in the Kuiper belt.

title: Far side of the Moon
why: China's Chang'e 4 makes the first soft landing on the far side of the Moon.

title: Black hole image
why: The Event Horizon Telescope reveals the first image of a black hole, the shadow of the giant one at the center of galaxy M87.

title: Sensitivity conjecture
why: Hao Huang settles, in a two-page proof, a 30-year-old computer science question about how strongly a yes-or-no rule reacts when one of its inputs is flipped.

title: Ebola treatments
why: A trial in Congo shows that two antibody drugs, mAb114 and REGN-EB3, sharply cut deaths from Ebola, the first treatments proven to do so.

title: Fast radio bursts
why: A radio telescope catches a fast radio burst from a magnetar inside our own galaxy, revealing for the first time what produces these millisecond flashes.

title: Dexamethasone
why: A cheap steroid becomes the first drug shown to save lives from COVID-19, cutting deaths by up to a third in a trial led by Peter Horby and Martin Landray.

title: COVID-19 vaccines
why: An mRNA vaccine from Uğur Şahin and Özlem Türeci's BioNTech and Pfizer prevents more than 90% of COVID-19 cases, less than a year after the virus appeared.

title: Ingenuity
why: NASA's Ingenuity helicopter makes the first powered, controlled flight on another planet, hovering above Mars for 39 seconds.

title: Complete human genome
why: A team led by Karen Miga and Adam Phillippy posts the first truly complete human genome, filling the 8% left unread since 2001.

title: In-body gene editing
why: CRISPR given by infusion edits genes inside patients' bodies for the first time, cutting a disease-causing protein by up to 96%, in results reported by Julian Gillmore's team.

title: Malaria vaccine
why: The WHO recommends RTS,S for African children, the first vaccine against malaria and against any human parasite.

title: Pig heart transplant
org: University of Maryland School of Medicine
why: Surgeons Bartley Griffith and Muhammad Mohiuddin give a living man, David Bennett, a gene-edited pig heart, the first such transplant.

title: Kahn–Kalai conjecture
why: Jinyoung Park and Huy Tuan Pham prove, in a strikingly short paper, a major 2006 conjecture about when random networks suddenly gain a given structure.

title: Sagittarius A*
why: A worldwide network of radio telescopes takes the first image of the black hole at the center of our galaxy.

title: Asteroid deflection
why: NASA confirms that crashing its DART spacecraft into the asteroid Dimorphos shortened its orbit by 32 minutes, the first time people have changed a celestial body's motion.

title: Fusion ignition
why: A fusion experiment at Lawrence Livermore's National Ignition Facility releases more energy than its lasers deliver to the fuel, a first for controlled fusion.

title: Ramsey numbers
org: IMPA, PUC-Rio and University of Cambridge
why: Four mathematicians make the first exponential improvement since 1935 on how big a network must be to guarantee a group that is either fully connected or fully disconnected.

title: Aperiodic monotile
org: University of Waterloo and University of Arkansas
why: Hobbyist David Smith finds the "hat," the first single shape that tiles a flat surface only in a pattern that never repeats.

title: Gravitational-wave background
org: NANOGrav and other pulsar timing arrays
why: Fifteen years of timing pulsars give evidence of a faint hum of gravitational waves filling the universe, likely from pairs of giant black holes.

title: GLP-1 obesity drugs
why: Semaglutide, built on GLP-1 hormone research by Joel Habener, Svetlana Mojsov and Lotte Bjerre Knudsen, becomes the first weight-loss drug shown to cut heart attacks, strokes and heart deaths, by 20%.

title: CRISPR therapy
why: UK regulators approve Casgevy for sickle cell disease, the first approved medicine made with CRISPR.

title: Pig kidney transplant
why: Surgeons led by Tatsuo Kawai and Leonardo Riella give Rick Slayman the first gene-edited pig kidney transplanted into a living person.

title: Geometric Langlands conjecture
org: Max Planck Institute for Mathematics and Yale University
why: A nine-person team led by Dennis Gaitsgory and Sam Raskin posts an 800-page proof of a central piece of math's "grand unified theory."

title: Lenacapavir
why: A shot given twice a year prevents every HIV infection among more than 2,000 young women in Africa, in a trial led by Linda-Gail Bekker.

title: Lunar far side samples
why: China's Chang'e 6 brings the first rock and soil from the Moon's far side back to Earth.

title: Rocket booster catch
why: SpaceX catches its returning Super Heavy booster with its launch tower's arms, on the first try.

title: Kakeya conjecture in 3D
org: NYU and University of British Columbia
why: Hong Wang and Joshua Zahl prove the Kakeya conjecture in three dimensions, a decades-old question about how small a space can be if a needle inside it points in every direction.

title: 2D metals
org: Institute of Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences
why: A team led by Guangyu Zhang and Luojun Du squeezes molten metals such as bismuth into sheets a few atoms thick, the first two-dimensional metals.

title: Personalized gene editing
org: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia and Penn Medicine
why: Kiran Musunuru and Rebecca Ahrens-Nicklas build a gene-editing therapy for one baby, KJ Muldoon, correcting the single DNA letter behind his deadly liver disease.

title: Huntington's disease
why: A one-time gene therapy, AMT-130, tested with Sarah Tabrizi, becomes the first treatment shown to slow Huntington's disease, by 75% over three years.

title: Self-copying RNA
why: Edoardo Gianni and Philipp Holliger find a 45-letter RNA molecule that can build both itself and its partner strand, the closest yet to the self-copying molecule thought to have started life.

title: Daraxonrasib
why: A daily pill that blocks the RAS cancer gene doubles survival in advanced pancreatic cancer, from 6.7 to 13.2 months.

title: Habitable-zone atmosphere
why: Astronomers led by Collin Cherubim detect helium escaping LHS 1140 b, the first sign of an atmosphere on a rocky planet in its star's habitable zone.
